name: Stabilization Artifact
description: Profiles camera motion trajectories and stabilization residuals to distinguish authentic handheld footage from AI-generated video exhibiting either unrealistic steadiness or synthetic motion patterns.
mechanism:
This method detects video stabilization artifacts for forensic analysis:

1. **Camera Motion Estimation**: Global camera motion is estimated from background feature tracking — translation, rotation, and zoom components per frame. The raw (unstabilized) camera motion trajectory is reconstructed.

2. **Stabilization Artifact Detection**: Video stabilization smooths camera motion by applying compensating transforms. This produces characteristic artifacts: (a) cropped borders (stabilization reduces effective field of view), (b) warping residuals from rolling shutter correction, (c) motion blur inconsistent with the displayed (stabilized) motion.

3. **Double Stabilization Detection**: If a deepfake video is stabilized and then the original footage was also stabilized, double-stabilization produces characteristic artifacts: excessive border cropping, over-smoothed motion (unnatural zero jitter), and cumulative warping residuals.

4. **Face-Background Motion Consistency**: After de-stabilization, the apparent motion of the face and background should be consistent with the same camera motion. If the face was generated and composited, its motion may not match the camera motion recovered from the background, creating a detectable motion inconsistency.

5. **Stabilization History Analysis**: The method estimates whether and how many times the video was stabilized. Each stabilization pass leaves a characteristic imprint on the motion trajectory (reduced high-frequency components). Multiple stabilization passes indicate the video has been processed multiple times — consistent with a manipulation → re-stabilization pipeline.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through stabilization artifact analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Amerini, I. et al. (2019). Deepfake Video Detection through Optical Flow based CNN. ICCV Workshop.
Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
